ideas.title: Get Paid to Care: Family Caregiver Enrollment
ideas.one_liner: A navigator that gets family caregivers onto Medicaid and VA payrolls, then becomes the fiscal intermediary that pays them.
ideas.customer: Adult children and spouses (45-70) giving 20+ hours a week of unpaid care to a low-income parent or veteran. Secondary buyers are Area Agencies on Aging, Medicaid managed-care plans and state Medicaid agencies that pay fiscal-intermediary fees.
ideas.problem: 59M family caregivers gave 49.5B unpaid hours in 2024 (about $1T) and lose roughly $21k a year in income. Every state has Medicaid self-direction, many pay relatives, and the VA has Veteran-Directed Care. But the rules differ by state, the assessment sets the hours, and agencies and fiscal intermediaries earn more by placing an outside aide.
ideas.solution: Phase 1 is a state-by-state 'can I get paid?' screener plus done-with-you enrollment: eligibility, application packet, coaching for the nurse assessment (which sets hours), employee onboarding, timesheet and electronic-visit-verification coaching, and appeals. Phase 2 is to become a licensed fiscal intermediary (payroll, background checks, EVV) in states that allow several vendors, and to bill the state a monthly per-participant fee.
ideas.why_now: About $911B in federal Medicaid cuts plus work requirements, 41 states with HCBS waitlists over 600k people (average wait 15 months), and Wisconsin agencies 'not able to take new clients' after the 2026 visa and TPS shocks. States now have to lean on the caregiver already in the house.
ideas.revenue_model: Families pay a flat $349-499 per successful enrollment, or a lower fee plus a first-year success fee. Phase 2 adds state or MCO fiscal-intermediary per-member-per-month fees. AAAs can pay for referral-sourced enrollment.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The shortage is partly a payment-eligibility problem, not a bodies problem. The gatekeepers who could help families avoid agencies are the agencies and legacy fiscal intermediaries, so no one with a business incentive teaches families the paid-relative pathway.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick two states where relatives can be paid and enrollment is open (California's IHSS is the obvious one). Publish the screener and state guides, then capture leads through caregiver support groups, Facebook groups and elder-law firms. Sell a $349 concierge enrollment to the first 20 families and measure approval rate and approved hours.

ideas.title: Shared-Aide Pods for 55+ Apartment Buildings
ideas.one_liner: One on-site aide team serves 6-10 residents in the same building, delivering assisted-living-style help at a fraction of 1:1 home-care cost.
ideas.customer: Owners and operators of independent-living and 55+ apartment buildings (market-rate, senior LIHTC and HUD-202 properties). The payers are middle-income residents and their families, who can't afford $75-130k a year and are stuck on waitlists.
ideas.problem: Home care is sold as one aide per client per hour ($35 an hour, about $80k a year for 44 hours a week) only because of legacy billing. Assisted living is at 90% occupancy with almost no new supply before 2030. Residents who age past independent living either move out or go without.
ideas.solution: A licensed home-care agency subsidiary (or partnership with one) posts 2-3 aides per shift inside the building. They run scheduled 15-45 minute ADL, medication-reminder, meal-setup and toileting visits, plus overnight response. Dispatch software handles acuity tiers and in-building routing (floors, elevators). Residents buy monthly tiers of about $1,800-3,500, and the property gets a retention amenity.
ideas.why_now: NIC MAP shows 57 of 99 metros above 90% occupancy, units under construction at a 2012 low, and no meaningful new supply before 2030. Medicaid HCBS is walled off by 15-month waitlists and labor is scarcer after the 2026 visa pause, so stretching each aide across more clients is the only lever left.
ideas.revenue_model: Monthly resident subscription by care tier, with a revenue share or amenity fee to the property owner. Later, Medicaid HCBS or managed-care billing for pods in affordable senior buildings.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Aide hours are cheap to make dense (no drive time, no client-hour minimums) but are priced as if they were mobile. The gap between 1:1 pricing and 1:8 cost is the whole business, and only a property-anchored operator can capture it. Assisted-living-without-the-license is a real category nobody has scaled.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign a 90-day pilot with one 100-200 unit 55+ property in a tight market. Subcontract to an existing licensed agency to move quickly, staff a two-aide pod, and target 15 residents at about $2,200 a month. Track aide minutes per resident and move-out avoidance.

ideas.title: Turnkey Six-Bed Care Homes for Nurse-Operators
ideas.one_liner: A licensing-and-operations platform that turns ordinary houses into small licensed residential care homes run by nurses and experienced aides.
ideas.customer: Nurses, CNAs and senior aides (including immigrant health workers) who want to own and run a home, plus small investors and families who own a suitable house.
ideas.problem: Insiders think the senior-housing gap ($275B, about 549k units by 2028) needs towers, REIT capital and 3-5 year development. Yet many states license 4-10 bed homes in normal single-family zoning. The barriers are licensing know-how, fire and ADA retrofits, staffing plans and a steady flow of admissions, not capital.
ideas.solution: A 90-day licensing sprint: zoning and state licensing packet, retrofit checklist, insurance, policies and procedures. Then staffing playbooks (1:3 to 1:6 ratios), charting, medication and compliance software, an admissions pipeline from hospital discharge planners who can't find beds, and financing partners (HELOC, sale-leaseback, small-investor pools). Start with states that have small-home license categories (for example Washington adult family homes, Arizona assisted-living homes and California small RCFEs).
ideas.why_now: Occupancy is at 90.1%, the highest since 2007. Inventory growth was 0.4% in Q1 2026, the lowest on record, and nothing new arrives before 2030. Hospital discharge teams are desperate for beds, and seniors hold a record $14.92T in home equity.
ideas.revenue_model: $6-12k onboarding fee per home, 5-8% management or software fee on revenue, and a placement fee from families where permitted. Later a captive group-purchasing and insurance program.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Supply can appear in 6 months if the constraint is permission and playbooks, not concrete. One nurse-operator with a 5-bedroom house at $5-7k per resident per month can rival a mid-size facility's per-bed economics with no construction.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 10 prospective operators through nursing-school and CNA Facebook groups. Sell a $2,500 feasibility-and-licensing sprint, publish a 'how to license a six-bed home in [state]' guide as lead-gen, and line up one hospital discharge planner as a first referral source.

ideas.title: Care-First Reverse Mortgages With Locked Payouts
ideas.one_liner: A care-planning broker that funds long-term care from home equity and releases the money only to verified caregivers and facilities.
ideas.customer: Homeowners 70-85 with $300k+ equity and thin liquid savings, or their adult children holding a power of attorney. The channel is elder-law attorneys, geriatric care managers and hospital discharge planners.
ideas.problem: Long-term-care insurance is failing policyholders: Genworth has about $31.8B of approved premium hikes, and 2023 hikes averaged 51%. Care runs $75-115k a year, and Medicaid retrenchment is coming. The one big asset is home equity, but advisors still treat reverse mortgages as a last resort and lump sums invite fraud and sibling fights.
ideas.solution: Start with a 12-month care budget and plan. Match it to a reverse-mortgage line of credit (HECM or proprietary), through an NMLS-licensed broker or a co-brokering partner. Then open a care wallet: funds go only to vetted payees (agency, facility, or a family caregiver under a documented personal-care agreement with payroll), with a ledger for siblings and Medicaid look-back records, and multi-party approval for any other outflow.
ideas.why_now: Proprietary reverse mortgages now hold 52% share against 48% for HECM, so products are better. Seniors hold $14.92T in home equity. LTC insurance is unravelling, the 80+ cohort is exploding, and elder fraud hit $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), which makes lump-sum liquidity risky without controls.
ideas.revenue_model: Broker origination compensation on funded loans, roughly 1-2% of loan amount, plus a $49 a month care-wallet fee. Licensing the wallet to lenders as a fraud-protection differentiator is later upside.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The product isn't the loan; it's controlled disbursement plus a care plan. Reverse mortgages are viewed with suspicion because of how the cash gets spent, and a locked, audited payout stream fixes the exact failure mode that ruined the category's reputation.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with a licensed reverse-mortgage broker, publish 'how to pay for care with home equity' content, and build referral relationships with 10 elder-law firms and care managers. Loans close in about 60-75 days, so first revenue lands inside six months.

ideas.title: Certify Overseas Eldercare, Insure the Trip Home
ideas.one_liner: An independent audit standard, trial-stay program and medevac-backed membership for Americans moving parents into care in Mexico, the Philippines or Thailand.
ideas.customer: Adult children and spouses of middle-income seniors (assets $50-150k) who can't afford $6,300 a month in the US and can't get Medicaid. Elder-law and financial planners are the channel, and overseas operators buy audits.
ideas.problem: Assisted living and memory care abroad run $800-3,000 a month with 1:3 to 1:5 staffing claims, but there is no independent quality standard, Medicare doesn't work abroad, and families have no emergency evacuation or continuity-of-care plan. Trust, not price, blocks the market.
ideas.solution: US-run unannounced audits by bilingual RNs against a published rubric (staff ratios, medication safety, dementia protocols, fire, hospital proximity), with public scorecards. Add a 30-day trial-stay package, a membership bundling medevac and repatriation cover from a partner, US-physician telehealth oversight, and a family-visit travel budget.
ideas.why_now: The 2026 visa pause and TPS terminations closed the door on importing workers, and Wisconsin nursing homes wrote off apartments bought for overseas hires. Labor now moves the other way: patients go to the labor. Alongside the US costs ($114,975 a year for a nursing home, $74,400 for assisted living) and 90% occupancy, families are already exploring it.
ideas.revenue_model: Family-paid vetting and placement fee of $750-2,500 (families only, to avoid conflicts), $600-1,200 a year membership for evacuation cover and telehealth oversight, and separate operator-paid annual audit subscriptions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Nobody thinks seniors will leave the US, but the buyer is a middle-income family choosing between $115k a year and a waitlist. The moat is a trusted third-party scorecard and a way home, the same trust layer that made medical tourism scalable.
ideas.first_30_days: Visit and score 10 facilities in one cluster (for example Lake Chapala/Guadalajara) with a nurse partner. Publish the rubric and first scorecards, pre-sell 30-day trial-stay packages to expat and retire-abroad groups, and sign a medevac partner.

ideas.title: Home-Readiness Crews for Hospital-at-Home Programs
ideas.one_liner: On-call crews that make a patient's home hospital-ready in hours and provide a non-clinical overnight presence for the first 72 hours.
ideas.customer: Hospital-at-Home program directors at health systems, and Medicare Advantage plans and ACOs that fund them.
ideas.problem: Extending the waiver lets programs scale, but many referred patients get screened out because of clutter, stairs, pets, bad Wi-Fi or power, no bedside space, or no adult present overnight. Every screen-out is a lost admission that would have replaced $2,500+ inpatient days. No one owns the home itself.
ideas.solution: A van and two-person crew does a rapid home assessment (power, connectivity via hotspot or eSIM, safe path, bedside setup, hazard removal, DME handoff). A vetted sitter provides overnight presence and escalates to the nurse line, and the crew resets the home at discharge. An address-based readiness score pre-screens referrals before the ED sends them.
ideas.why_now: The Hospital-at-Home waiver was extended five years, to Sep 30, 2030, so systems are committing capital and hiring. 80+ growth and 90% occupancy in senior housing mean more frail patients whose homes are the constraint.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-episode fee of $350-900 plus monthly retainers for guaranteed response, and a software license for the readiness score.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource isn't clinicians or tech; it's a safe physical environment and a body in the room at 3 am. Whoever solves 'make the home hospital-grade' raises hospital-at-home conversion rates, which is what programs are judged on.
ideas.first_30_days: Pitch three hospital-at-home directors and offer a pilot at cost on 20 episodes, using existing local caregiver and sitter pools. Track screen-out conversion and cost per episode.

ideas.title: Professional Health-Care Agents for Solo Agers
ideas.one_liner: A subscription 'designated agent' nurse-advocate with health-care proxy authority who is reachable at 2 am, sold to solo agers and to hospitals stuck with unbefriended patients.
ideas.customer: Solo agers 70-85 with $300k-$2M in assets and no spouse or children nearby (27% of 65+ live alone). Hospitals and elder-law attorneys are the B2B channels.
ideas.problem: Solo agers often lack a health-care proxy. When a crisis hits, hospitals face consent and discharge bottlenecks, and the state may appoint a professional guardian through a slow, expensive court process. Agencies and hospitals can't act as trusted agents because of conflicts of interest.
ideas.solution: A nurse- or social-worker-led firm whose individual employees serve as named health-care agents. It handles values interviews and updated directives, a wallet card and QR code hospitals can scan to reach the on-call agent, monthly check-ins, and in-hospital advocacy during admissions and discharge. It coordinates with a separate financial fiduciary. AI documentation tools let one agent serve 60-80 clients. Hospitals can also contract for surrogate support for unbefriended patients.
ideas.why_now: Solo-ager demographics and the 80+ cohort are surging (NPR, Jul 2026). SNF and home-care capacity is tightening, so discharge delays cost hospitals more, and family caregivers are stretched by Medicaid retrenchment.
ideas.revenue_model: $2,400-4,800 a year subscription plus hourly rates for hospital stays, and $1,500-3,000 per unbefriended-patient episode from hospitals.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Care is available if you can pay, but a trusted person with legal authority who answers at 2 am is the missing product. Because family-based caregiving is the default assumption, almost every caregiver product targets a family that doesn't exist for this cohort.
ideas.first_30_days: In one state with friendly proxy law (Washington, Oregon or Colorado), recruit two RN or MSW advocates, sign 10 clients through estate attorneys, and approach two hospital case-management directors with a pilot for unbefriended patients.

ideas.title: Vacant-House Concierge for Parents Moving Into Care
ideas.one_liner: One monthly plan that insures, inspects, maintains and eventually sells the house left empty when a parent moves to memory care or dies.
ideas.customer: Adult children and executors (45-65), often out of state, acting under POA or as executor. The channels are elder-law and estate attorneys, memory-care sales directors and senior move managers.
ideas.problem: When a parent moves into care, the house sits empty for 3-12 months. Homeowners policies typically restrict coverage after 30-60 days of vacancy, and pipes, taxes, utilities, break-ins and mail scams pile up. Probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024, and exhausted heirs are unprepared.
ideas.solution: A $199-449 monthly plan: vacancy-compliant insurance via an MGA partner, weekly inspections with water, temperature and entry sensors, autopay of utilities, taxes and HOA from an estate or POA account, seasonal maintenance, mail forwarding, sibling portal, documentation for the estate accounting, then cleanout, staging and a sell-when-ready referral.
ideas.why_now: The 80+ cohort is growing about 36.6% over the decade, senior housing is at 90% occupancy so moves happen in crises, and the $6T wealth transfer is underway. Heirs are far-flung Gen X executors who need a service, not a checklist.
ideas.revenue_model: Monthly subscription, insurance commissions, cleanout and staging fees, and a referral or flat fee on the eventual sale.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Estate-settlement startups start at death, but the costly, uninsured window opens at the care move, years earlier. Anchoring on that moment gives access to the family before competitors and before the house loses value.
ideas.first_30_days: In one metro dense with senior housing, recruit 10 estate and elder-law attorneys and five move managers, secure a vacancy-insurance MGA quote, and sign the first 10 homes at an introductory rate.

ideas.title: 30-Day Capacity-Window Plan After Early Alzheimer's Diagnosis
ideas.one_liner: A productized sprint that uses the legally competent window after an early blood-test diagnosis to lock down legal, financial, safety and care plans.
ideas.customer: Newly diagnosed patients and their spouses or adult children, reached through memory clinics, neurology and primary-care practices, blood-test labs and elder-law firms. Employers with caregiver benefits are a secondary buyer.
ideas.problem: Blood tests cleared in 2025 mean many people learn they're on the path to dementia while still competent, with a 3-7 year window to sign POAs, choose agents, set financial guardrails, plan driving and firearm safety, decide on Leqembi and record wishes. After capacity is lost, it becomes a court fight. CMS GUIDE closed enrollment after one 2024 window, so nobody owns the first 30 days.
ideas.solution: A fixed-fee, nurse-navigator-led sprint: a capacity-timed legal package via partner attorneys (POAs, directives, HIPAA releases, updated will or trust), financial guardrails (bill-pay automation, bank trusted-contact, scam locks), a safety plan (driving, firearms, stove, wandering), a care roadmap with cost projections and a Leqembi decision aid, and 90 days of dyad coaching.
ideas.why_now: FDA cleared Lumipulse pTau217 in May 2025 and a second primary-care blood test in Oct 2025. Leqembi Q1 sales rose 74% to $168M and it now has an at-home subcutaneous starting dose. Diagnosis is decentralizing while post-diagnosis coordination is not.
ideas.revenue_model: $1,500-3,500 fixed family fee, plus employer or LTC-insurer contracts. No referral payments from providers, to stay clear of anti-kickback issues.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Earlier diagnosis is a legal-capacity clock, not just a medical event. The valuable window is the one when the patient can still sign, and every document signed in it prevents a $5-15k guardianship later.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with two memory clinics and three elder-law firms, and deliver five pilot sprints at $1,500 each. Track documents executed while competent and family satisfaction.

ideas.title: Master-Leased Housing to Recruit Care Workers Domestically
ideas.one_liner: Asset-light staff housing near care facilities that lets operators recruit domestic workers from a wider radius, starting with stranded worker apartments.
ideas.customer: Nursing homes, assisted-living and memory-care operators (5-40 sites) and home-care agencies in tight labor markets such as Wisconsin and rural areas.
ideas.problem: The visa pause cuts off the overseas pipeline. Direct care workers are paid little (66% earn under $35k), so domestic recruits can't afford to relocate to where beds are staffed. Closed beds and wings in Wisconsin show the cost. Turnover of 77-80% means every hire has to be retained.
ideas.solution: Master-lease or take over apartments near facilities, furnish them, and sublease bed by bed to employees at below-market rent. Employers fund the gap ($300-600 per bed per month) under a guarantee. Add a 3-month 'landing pad' with transport, CNA certification and ESL classes, and a relocation pipeline from oversupplied labor markets (laid-off retail and hospitality workers).
ideas.why_now: Wisconsin nursing homes spent $100k+ on apartments for overseas workers and then abandoned the plan when visa access closed, so there are stranded assets to take over. About 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4, and about one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-bed monthly management margin ($100-200 on top of rent), employer subsidy, and a $1,500 placement fee per hire retained at 90 days.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: When foreign labor is cut off, housing rather than wages becomes the binding constraint to domestic recruitment. A 20-bed closed wing loses over $1M a year in revenue, so a $7k a year housing subsidy per worker is trivially worth it.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach the Wisconsin operators who bought apartments and offer to operate and re-let them to domestic hires. Run a 12-bed pilot in one town with two operators and track time-to-fill and 90-day retention.

ideas.title: Worker-Ownership Succession for Home Care Agencies
ideas.one_liner: A specialist shop that helps retiring home-care agency owners sell to their caregivers via an ESOP or worker co-op, plus a shared back office for the converted agencies.
ideas.customer: Owners aged 58-72 of $2-15M revenue home-care agencies with no successor. CDFI lenders and employee-ownership funds are financing partners.
ideas.problem: Reimbursement is squeezed (a 1.3% aggregate cut for CY2026, with a -3.0% temporary adjustment still in place), private-equity money goes to software and big platforms, and even UnitedHealth had to divest 164 Amedisys locations. Small owners have no buyer, while agencies lose 77-80% of caregivers a year.
ideas.solution: A conversion shop: valuation, readiness (licensure and payer change-of-ownership rules), structure (S-corp ESOP, worker co-op or employee-ownership trust), financing (seller note plus CDFI or SBA), and a two-year ownership-culture program (caregiver equity, profit sharing, scheduling voice). Converted agencies share a back office (payroll, billing, EVV, recruiting).
ideas.why_now: Boomer owners are retiring into a weak sales market after the 2026 rate squeeze, and the workforce shortage means the workforce is the scarcest asset. Cooperative Home Care Associates in the Bronx shows the model works.
ideas.revenue_model: Transaction fee of 3-5% of deal value, $8-15k a month back-office fees, and a small share of network EBITDA.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: In a business where turnover is the profit killer, the best buyer for a struggling agency is the workforce itself. Ownership is a retention tool, and the exit-plan angle sells to owners who don't care about culture.
ideas.first_30_days: Work with a state home-care association to get 20 owner conversations. Sell five $12k ownership-readiness assessments, line up a CDFI lender, and target first LOI within six months.

ideas.title: Court-Accounting Software for Family Conservators and Executors
ideas.one_liner: Statement-to-court-form automation for family members who must file annual accountings for a parent under conservatorship or through probate.
ideas.customer: Lay conservators, guardians and executors (Gen X children), plus probate attorneys, CPAs and professional fiduciaries who handle 20-200 cases.
ideas.problem: Roughly a million-plus adults are under guardianship or conservatorship, and probate cases rose about 32% from 2020 to 2024. Appointed family members must file county- and state-specific accountings with receipts and categories. Errors mean surcharges or removal, and lawyers or accountants charge $500-2,500 a filing.
ideas.solution: Connect bank accounts or upload statements, categorize against the state's court forms, flag court-sensitive items (gifts, related-party payments, unusual withdrawals), produce the accounting and receipt binder, and calendar deadlines. Include optional attorney review. Launch in California and Texas, where forms and rules are standardized.
ideas.why_now: 80+ growth means more incapacity and more estates. Elder fraud losses ($7.7B in 2025) are pushing courts to scrutinize guardians, and LLMs now parse statements accurately enough for categorization.
ideas.revenue_model: $399 a year per case for lay fiduciaries, and $79-150 per case per month for professional fiduciaries and law firms.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Legal tech serves lawyers and estate-planning creation; nobody serves the family member who is legally required to be an amateur accountant. Court deadlines make the pain acute and the willingness to pay high.
ideas.first_30_days: Start with California and Texas. Build SEO around 'conservatorship accounting help', partner with probate attorneys, and sell the first 20 cases at $399.

ideas.title: Outsourced Elder-Exploitation Desk for Credit Unions
ideas.one_liner: A managed service where trained specialists take flagged older-member transactions, call the member and trusted contact, file reports and document compliance.
ideas.customer: Community banks and credit unions ($300M-$5B in assets) with older memberships. Sales run through CUSOs, state leagues and core-processor marketplaces to BSA and fraud officers.
ideas.problem: Americans 60+ reported $7.7B in fraud losses in 2025 (up 59%), with an average loss over $38k and 12,400+ people losing $100k or more. Small institutions have alerts but no trained humans to call members, coordinate lawful holds, file SARs and APS reports, and prove Senior Safe Act training.
ideas.solution: Ingest the institution's flagged-alert queue and staff a desk with retired bank fraud investigators and social workers who use scripts to break the scam spell (pig-butchering, crypto-ATM, impostor). The desk coordinates holds, files APS and SAR narratives, runs annual Senior Safe Act training, and delivers quarterly avoided-loss analytics.
ideas.why_now: Investment and pig-butchering fraud is over a third of losses, older adults are adopting AI fast (23% of 65+ use ChatGPT, up from 10%), and voice-cloning scams raise stakes. State attorneys general and regulators are pressing institutions to do more.
ideas.revenue_model: $2-6k a month per institution by asset size, plus per-case fees, sold on documented avoided loss.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Consumer fraud apps are crowded, but the institution is the party with a duty of care, and the missing capacity is human case handling, not another detection model. Pricing to avoided losses makes the ROI obvious.
ideas.first_30_days: Sell a 90-day pilot to two credit unions through a CUSO or state league, staffed by two retired fraud investigators and a social worker. Record prevented losses and hold-to-report cycle time.

ideas.title: Waiver-Funded Home Modification Back Office and Factoring
ideas.one_liner: Handle the prior-authorization paperwork and advance payment for small contractors who do ramps and bathroom retrofits funded by Medicaid waivers and VA grants.
ideas.customer: Small accessibility and remodeling contractors (3-15 employees) in states with waiver home-modification benefits, plus case managers and AAAs who can't find bidders.
ideas.problem: Senior housing supply is stuck through 2030, so aging in place is structurally favored and home mods are the cheapest fix. But waiver and VA HISA funding needs OT assessments, multiple bids, packets, inspections and 60-120 day payment, so good contractors avoid it. Approved seniors can't find anyone to do the work.
ideas.solution: A back office that prepares the packet (OT evaluation scheduling, standard scope, photos, bids, permits), tracks approval, submits invoices, and advances 85-90% of payment within five days against the approved authorization. A network directory shows case managers which contractors are ready to bid.
ideas.why_now: 41 states have HCBS waitlists over 600k, so states favor cheap home-based solutions over $115k-a-year nursing home stays. Medicaid cuts and 15-month waits add pressure, while 80+ growth means demand for mods is up.
ideas.revenue_model: 3-5% packet fee, a 1.5-3% factoring spread, and a platform fee from states or MCOs for a ready-to-bid contractor pool.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck for funded home modifications is contractor cash flow and paperwork, not consumer demand or budget. Fixing the contractor's experience creates supply where the money already exists.
ideas.first_30_days: In one state, recruit five contractors and process 10 packets. Secure a small credit line from a CDFI or SBA lender to fund advances, then approach the state's HCBS case management office.

ideas.title: Work-Authorization Continuity Benefit for Care Employers
ideas.one_liner: An employer-paid benefit that screens every care worker for legal pathways, tracks EAD renewals and reverification, and plans backfill.
ideas.customer: Home-care agencies, nursing homes and assisted-living groups with 50-2,000 workers, especially in NY, FL, MA, MN, WI and CA, and staffing agencies.
ideas.problem: 30% of direct care workers are immigrants (60% in New York), and about 350,000 Haitians lost TPS on Aug 4. At least one in five immigrant direct-care workers come from countries hit by the 75-country visa pause. With turnover already at 77-80%, losing staff means closed beds, and few workers have been screened for family, asylum, adjustment or other pathways.
ideas.solution: A per-worker monthly benefit: confidential attorney-led status screening and pathway triage, EAD and renewal tracking with on-time filing, an I-9 reverification calendar with non-discriminatory templates, workforce-at-risk forecasting by site and date, and fast backfill through a partner training school. Employers see aggregate risk, not individual status.
ideas.why_now: The 2026 visa pause, TPS terminations and a DOL proposal to roll back home-care wage protections hit at once, and Wisconsin agencies say they're 'just not able to take new clients.' Employers need something other than lobbying.
ideas.revenue_model: $8-15 per worker per month (employer-paid), plus filing fees with 20-30% margin and optional filing-fee financing.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Immigration compliance is treated as static HR paperwork, but for care employers it is now a retention and continuity problem. Attorney-led screening can surface pathways that keep workers, which is worth thousands per retained caregiver.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with an immigration law firm and a Haitian community organization, sign three agencies with Haitian-heavy workforces (NY, FL, MA), and pilot with 200 workers.

ideas.title: Remote-Piloted Care Robots: Labor by Teleoperation
ideas.one_liner: Mobile manipulators supervised by remote pilots handle non-clinical night-shift chores in memory care, importing labor by bandwidth instead of visa.
ideas.customer: Memory-care and assisted-living operators (night and evening shifts), later affluent solo agers at home. The buyer is the operations executive with a labor budget.
ideas.problem: Night ratios of about 1:20 mean chores (water rounds, linen, trash, fetching supplies) compete with clinical rounds. Every open aide slot costs $45-60k with overtime. The 2026 visa pause closes the foreign-labor route.
ideas.solution: Off-the-shelf mobile manipulators (a Hello Robot Stretch-class robot, about $25k, and later humanoids) supervised by a bilingual remote pilot network trained on non-clinical tasks, with one pilot overseeing 3-4 robots. The first product is a night-shift runner: water and linen rounds, trash, fetch, room tidy, and a face-and-voice response to call lights that routes to a human aide. No lifting of residents and no clinical tasks.
ideas.why_now: Consumer humanoids with human-teleop fallback (1X's NEO opened preorders in late 2025), cheap mobile manipulators and vision-language-action models make assisted autonomy feasible in 2026. Wisconsin nursing homes' failed overseas-labor plan shows demand for labor by any route.
ideas.revenue_model: Robot-as-a-service at about $4,500 a month per robot for 12 hours a day (roughly $12-15 an hour against a $28-35 loaded aide cost), plus implementation fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The moat is the pilot network, the safety case and the ops playbook, not the hardware. Teleoperation turns overseas labor into a service delivered without a visa, and a human-in-the-loop model works long before full autonomy.
ideas.first_30_days: Lease two Stretch-class robots and recruit six pilots from a Manila BPO. Run a free two-week night-shift pilot in one memory-care community, log chores and aide-minutes saved, and collect LOIs.

ideas.title: Portable MRI Vans for Alzheimer's Drug Safety Monitoring
ideas.one_liner: A mobile low-field MRI service that scans anti-amyloid patients at home or in memory-care communities for brain-swelling safety checks.
ideas.customer: Memory clinics, neurology practices and infusion centers running anti-amyloid therapy, plus health systems. Later, manufacturer patient-support programs and payers.
ideas.problem: Anti-amyloid drugs require serial MRI safety monitoring for ARIA (brain swelling or bleeding). Scheduling MRI slots is a hidden throttle, and frail 80-year-olds struggle with hospital scanner visits. With blood tests and at-home dosing widening the funnel, monitoring capacity is the next bottleneck.
ideas.solution: A tech plus a portable FDA-cleared low-field scanner (Hyperfine Swoop class) in a van or cart, with teleradiology reads scheduled around dosing. Start with a concordance study against 3T for ARIA-E and ARIA-H (early reports suggest low-field can flag such changes, but it needs validation), then contract per scan to clinics.
ideas.why_now: Leqembi Q1 sales rose 74% to $168M, with Eisai and Biogen expecting over $1B this year, a subcutaneous at-home starting dose is now cleared, and two blood tests are cleared. Portable MRI and AI reconstruction have matured.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-scan fee of about $250-450 paid by clinics or manufacturer support programs, a per-patient monitoring program subscription, and data licensing for post-marketing studies.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The market talks about drug and diagnosis, but scan capacity and patient logistics decide throughput. The regulatory and reimbursement path is uncertain, so the study itself is the first product and creates the evidence moat.
ideas.first_30_days: Contact five memory clinics with anti-amyloid volume, lease a portable scanner, design a 40-patient concordance study with an IRB and neuroradiologists, and ask the drug makers' patient-support programs for pilot funding.

ideas.title: Sundowning Night Companion Speaking in Family's Voice
ideas.one_liner: A bedside device that detects night waking and reorients a person with dementia in a voice they consented to, escalating to a caregiver or remote night aide.
ideas.customer: Family caregivers of people with moderate dementia at home (about 15% provide 60+ hours a week), memory-care communities with thin night ratios, and home-care agencies with overnight cases.
ideas.problem: Night waking is a top reason families place a loved one. Overnight aides cost $300-450 a night, and families otherwise absorb 3 am crises. Generic AI companions are seen as deceptive or are not built for dementia.
ideas.solution: A bedside speaker or tablet with radar or audio wake detection plays short, clinically scripted reorientation lines in a familiar voice (for example a spouse or child), seeded by a 'voice will' the person records and approves while they still have capacity. It escalates to the caregiver's phone with two-way voice, then to a paid remote night aide, and logs sleep patterns for the neurologist. Guardrails: no impersonation of the deceased, and clinician sign-off.
ideas.why_now: Voice cloning from seconds of audio and on-device speech models are cheap in 2026. NY, FL and NJ are giving away ElliQ, showing public payers buy companionship tech, and 23% of 65+ now use ChatGPT, so acceptance is rising.
ideas.revenue_model: $199 hardware plus $39-59 a month for families, $30-50 per bed per month for memory care, and remote night-aide add-on fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Ethics is the product: an advance 'voice will' turns a controversial deception into a consented comfort, like an advance directive for how you want to be soothed. Night is the least automated and most expensive shift.
ideas.first_30_days: Build on a commodity smart speaker with scripted lines, recruit 10 families through Alzheimer's support groups and one neurologist, and measure night-waking events over four weeks. Convene a geriatric psychiatrist and an ethicist as advisors.

ideas.title: Exosuit-as-a-Service Paid by Workers' Comp Carriers
ideas.one_liner: Rentable powered back-and-hip assist suits for home-care aides and nursing assistants, with usage data that earns workers' comp premium credits.
ideas.customer: Home-care agencies and nursing-home operators with high workers' comp experience mods, workers' comp carriers and MGAs with loss-control budgets, and PEOs.
ideas.problem: Aides and nursing assistants have some of the highest musculoskeletal injury rates, and a claim costs tens of thousands. Agencies can't install ceiling lifts in clients' homes, and with 77-80% turnover, injuries drive both cost and churn.
ideas.solution: Rent-by-month lightweight powered assist suits with sizing, training and warranty. Onboard sensors count bends and lifts to build injury-risk analytics for the carrier, who credits premiums. Start with clients who need transfers, and use it as a retention perk.
ideas.why_now: Consumer-priced powered exosuits appeared in 2025-26, and workforce scarcity makes worker safety and retention perks valuable. Comp carriers are actively looking for loss-control programs in a squeezed home-health margin environment.
ideas.revenue_model: $60-100 per suit per month paid by the agency or shared with the carrier, performance rebates, and an analytics subscription.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Sell to the party that pays for injuries (the carrier), not the aide, and let data turn a gadget into a premium negotiation. Lab claims of strain reduction still need real-world proof, which the pilot supplies.
ideas.first_30_days: Lease 30 suits from an OEM, find two agencies and a regional comp carrier, and run a 90-day trial measuring injuries, lost workdays and turnover.

ideas.title: Native-Language Translation Earpieces for Dementia Care
ideas.one_liner: Dementia-tuned real-time speech translation and a life-story phrasebook so aides can soothe residents in the language they reverted to.
ideas.customer: Memory-care communities and nursing homes with multilingual residents, and home-care agencies in NYC, Miami, LA, the Bay Area and Houston.
ideas.problem: People with dementia often revert to a first language, while 30% of care workers (60% in New York) are immigrants who speak other languages. The mismatch causes agitation, missed pain, more antipsychotic use and hospital transfers. Compliance-grade phone interpreters are too slow for a 3 am redirect.
ideas.solution: An earbud and tablet kit with speech-to-speech translation tuned for dementia (short, slow, warm, repetitive), a preloaded ADL and redirection phrasebook, resident life-story cards in their language (hometown, family, songs), and a video human-interpreter fallback within 30 seconds. Staff dashboards report agitation and PRN antipsychotic use.
ideas.why_now: Real-time on-device speech translation reached mainstream earbuds and phones in 2025-26, while visa and TPS shocks are replacing staff with workers who share fewer languages with residents.
ideas.revenue_model: $30-60 per resident per month, or $99 per aide per month, plus an implementation fee.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Language access is treated as a compliance checkbox, not a clinical tool. Generic translation isn't tuned to dementia speech and emotion, and the measurable outcome (fewer PRN antipsychotics) is a metric operators already care about.
ideas.first_30_days: Identify five memory-care communities with Spanish-, Russian- or Chinese-speaking residents. Run $500 pilots with tablets and an interpreter fallback, and measure PRN antipsychotic use before and after.

ideas.title: Agent Purchase Warranty: The Liability Layer
ideas.one_liner: Everyone is building payment rails for shopping agents. Nobody owns what happens when an agent buys the wrong thing, so sell the warranty and dispute layer.
ideas.customer: Startups building AI procurement and shopping agents for small businesses (office, restaurant and parts supplies), and the merchants those agents buy from. The first buyer is an agent vendor that wants merchants to accept its agent.
ideas.problem: Visa, Mastercard, Coinbase, Ripple and Stripe are all in agentic rails, and Visa and Mastercard joined Rain's alliance on 2026-08-18. Chargeback rules assume a human clicked buy. ISO's generative-AI exclusion is spreading across CGL policies, so when an agent orders 40 cases instead of 4, the merchant says it was authorized, the bank agrees, and the insurer excludes it.
ideas.solution: A mandate-versus-receipt adjudication API. The user's signed intent mandate (budget, item class, merchant allowlist) is logged. On a dispute, the API compares mandate, cart, receipt and delivery and pays valid claims automatically. The first version is a reserve-backed service warranty capped at $500-$2,000 per order, later fronted by an MGA and carrier. Merchants who accept mandate-logged agent orders get a 'warranted agent' signal that cuts false declines.
ideas.why_now: Agentic payments alliances formed in Aug 2026, DoorDash is live on Stripe/Tempo, and AI exclusions are appearing on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). Transaction volume is arriving just as coverage disappears.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-order warranty fee of about 0.4-1.0% of order value from the agent vendor or user. Merchant-side acceptance fee. Later, MGA commission once a carrier fronts the risk.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Rails are commodity and crowded, but liability allocation is what decides trust, just as Stripe won by absorbing fraud and disputes rather than moving bytes. Insurers exclude 'AI' generically because they have no data. A signed mandate log is exactly the data that lets a small underwriter price a slice they can't.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one SMB-procurement agent vendor. Offer a free mandate-log SDK plus a capped $50k reserve-backed warranty on its first 500 orders, and record dispute types and rates. Use that loss data to sign three similar vendors at about 0.75% per order.

ideas.title: Tariff Refund Recovery for Downstream Buyers
ideas.one_liner: Importers of record are collecting over $100B in tariff refunds, but the small businesses that paid tariff surcharges on their invoices are owed a share and nobody is collecting it for them.
ideas.customer: Mid-size US contractors, restaurant groups, retailers and manufacturers ($5M-$200M revenue) whose 2025-26 supplier invoices carried explicit tariff surcharges or tariff-attributed price increases.
ideas.problem: Refunds go to the importer of record, and many importers already passed the cost through. Downstream buyers may have contract or unjust-enrichment claims, but their AP teams never tracked surcharges. Small importers also find filing costly ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02), so cash sits with parties who have no incentive to share it.
ideas.solution: Connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite or the AP inbox and extract every invoice line mentioning a tariff or surcharge. Map each vendor to its importer of record using public import records. Estimate the refund-attributable share and generate demand packets with contract citations. A partner law firm handles escalations on contingency. Default settlement is a vendor credit memo, which preserves the relationship.
ideas.why_now: More than $100B has been refunded (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09), the government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo 2026-08-11), tariff lawsuits are surging, and 25 states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs. That means a second wave of surcharges to track.
ideas.revenue_model: 20-30% contingency on recovered cash or credits. After the first recovery, $299-$999 per month SaaS to track surcharges and refund clauses on future tariff swings.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Everyone is watching who receives the refund, and nobody watches who funded it. Many invoices literally say 'tariff surcharge, pass-through.' Vendors prefer credit memos to cash, so recoveries can be quiet and relationship-safe. The same invoice-clause tooling becomes a permanent tariff-swing shield.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 10 SMBs through trade associations and small-business communities and pull 24 months of AP exports. Run the analysis by hand with a lawyer's template letter and produce a $1M aggregate identified-claim demo. Sign two contingent agreements and send the first ten demand letters.

ideas.title: Scam Recovery Desk for Community Banks
ideas.one_liner: Banks buy scam detection, but the untapped money is recovery: stablecoin issuers, receiving banks and exchanges can freeze funds if someone asks fast and correctly.
ideas.customer: Community banks and credit unions ($500M-$10B assets) that increasingly eat scam reimbursements. American Banker (2026-07-22) puts bank-side scam losses at $68B, against the FTC's $15.9B of consumer-reported losses.
ideas.problem: A community bank's fraud analyst has hours before funds move on. They don't know who to call at receiving banks, exchanges or issuer compliance desks. They have no standard evidence pack, so recoveries run to a few percent and losses are written off as a cost of doing business.
ideas.solution: A 24/7 recovery desk plus software. When a victim reports a scam, the desk traces the funds (wire, Zelle and ACH recall, plus on-chain tracing for crypto off-ramps). It sends recall, 314(b) and law-enforcement freeze requests with pre-validated evidence packs to a maintained directory of receiving-institution and issuer contacts, then tracks outcomes. The desk is paid a share of every dollar recovered.
ideas.why_now: FTC losses hit a record $15.9B in 2025, and scam flows increasingly touch stablecoins. The Senate Democrats' Tether report (2026-09-28) raises pressure on issuers to respond quickly, and GENIUS-era issuers must be able to honor lawful freeze orders (verify exact text).
ideas.revenue_model: 15-25% contingency on recovered funds plus a flat monthly retainer for 24/7 coverage.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Recovery rates depend on speed and relationships, not analytics, so a maintained contact directory and playbook is an operations moat. Stablecoins are counterintuitively the most freezable scam rail, more so than wires or Zelle, if you know the freeze path.
ideas.first_30_days: Offer five community banks a free post-mortem of their last 90 days of scam cases and estimate the recoverable share. Hire two ex-bank fraud investigators. Sign two contingency pilots and build the first version of the issuer and receiving-bank contact directory.

ideas.title: Flood Cover Sold to the Lender
ideas.one_liner: Homeowners won't buy flood insurance, but the bank holding their mortgage should, because the uninsured flood loss lands on the lender's collateral.
ideas.customer: Community banks, credit unions and non-bank mortgage servicers with concentrated mortgage exposure outside FEMA high-risk zones, where flood cover isn't mandatory.
ideas.problem: Moody's puts uninsured US flood exposure at $375B-$1T. Private flood capacity is growing but 'customers aren't buying' (Insurance Business, 2026-07-22). Outside mandatory-purchase zones, borrowers skip cover, then walk or go delinquent after a flood and leave the lender with damaged collateral.
ideas.solution: Two steps. First, a parcel-level flood-exposure audit of the lender's book. Second, a lender-paid group or blanket flood policy (indemnity with a parametric fast-pay component) for the highest-risk non-mandatory loans, with disclosure and an opt-out. It is delivered as an MGA program on existing private flood capacity, and regulatory structure is validated state by state.
ideas.why_now: Private flood capacity is expanding (Neptune passed 300k policies and $400M premium). Reinsurance is softening, so capacity is cheap. Record cat bond issuance ($65.6B outstanding) shows abundant capital, and bank regulators are asking about climate concentration.
ideas.revenue_model: MGA commission and policy fees (roughly 10-20% of premium) plus a $15k-$40k paid portfolio audit per lender.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The demand problem is really a distribution problem. Selling to 10,000 skeptical homeowners is expensive, while selling to one lender covers thousands of borrowers. The party with the incentive to buy is the one who bears the unmandated loss.
ideas.first_30_days: Run free flood-exposure audits for 20 credit unions in river and Gulf states using public mortgage data and open flood models. Line up a licensed surplus-lines partner. Sell one paid pilot covering about 500 highest-risk loans.

ideas.title: Neighborhood Block Wildfire Cover via HOAs
ideas.one_liner: Softer reinsurance isn't reaching homeowners, so aggregate a mitigated neighborhood into one certified risk that capital will price like a portfolio instead of 300 anonymous parcels.
ideas.customer: HOA boards and Firewise-style communities of 200-2,000 homes in wildfire states (CA, CO, UT, NM, OR) where members are being nonrenewed or pushed to FAIR plans.
ideas.problem: Nonrenewals are at records and carriers price parcel by parcel, ignoring community-level mitigation like hydrants, vegetation control, ember vents and evacuation routes. Reinsurance is softening (Jefferies expects declines through 2027) but primary policyholders see none of it.
ideas.solution: Community risk certification, drone-verified and re-certified annually, plus block placement with an MGA or coverholder writing group-rated homeowner policies backed by reinsurance or ILS capital. The HOA collects dues, funds a shared deductible reserve and enforces mitigation standards.
ideas.why_now: California passed three claims and nonrenewal bills on 2026-09-03. Cat bond issuance is a record $18.9B year to date. Softening means capital is abundant and looking for well-defined books, and nonrenewals are a midterm political flashpoint.
ideas.revenue_model: MGA commission of about 12-15% of premium, $40-$100 per home for certification, and an HOA subscription for compliance tracking.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: In a soft market capital is abundant, and what's scarce is a verifiable, homogeneous risk pool. An HOA is a ready-made legal aggregator with dues collection and enforcement powers, which solves distribution and adverse selection together.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach 20 HOA management companies and Firewise sites in California foothills and Colorado's Front Range. Offer a free community risk-certification report. Sign one pilot LOI and line up an MGA willing to quote a block program.

ideas.title: Escrow Shock Early Warning for Servicers
ideas.one_liner: Soft reinsurance produces homeowner nonrenewals, which produce force-placed cover and escrow shortages, which produce delinquencies on servicers' books. Predict and defuse the shock before it lands.
ideas.customer: Mid-size mortgage servicers (50k-1M loans), including non-bank and credit-union servicers with loss-mitigation and hazard-insurance teams.
ideas.problem: Homeowner insurance now rivals mortgage payments (Tacoma News Tribune, Aug 2026). Nonrenewals hit records (Utah highest in 2025, New Mexico a record 6,200, county rate spikes up to 33% in H1 2026). When coverage lapses or moves to a FAIR plan, escrow analyses jump payments by hundreds of dollars a month and delinquencies follow.
ideas.solution: Score every loan for escrow-shock risk 90 days out, using state nonrenewal patterns, filed rate changes, tax data and the servicer's own hazard-insurance tracking. Then run assisted outreach before the shortage letter goes out: re-shop with an agent network, mitigation credits, and payment-plan options. Deliver dashboards and borrower-level outcomes to loss-mitigation heads.
ideas.why_now: Record nonrenewals, California's FAIR Plan taking more new loans (beinsure, Aug 2026), a HELOC surge signaling stretched households, and the household credit stress in the brief (record auto delinquencies, K-shaped economy).
ideas.revenue_model: $75-$200 per borrower resolved, or $0.50-$1.00 per loan per year SaaS. Optional share of avoided force-placed premium.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Servicers treat insurance as lapse-tracking compliance, not delinquency prevention. A single loss-mitigation case can cost hundreds of dollars, so even a 1% reduction in shock-driven delinquency pays for the product. Target servicers with investor and regulator pressure, since some earn money on force-placed cover.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a free escrow-shock heat map for three states from public data as a lead magnet. Cold-outreach loss-mitigation heads at 30 mid-size and credit-union servicers, and sign one pilot on about 20k loans.

ideas.title: Assisted Short Sales for Underwater Auto Loans
ideas.one_liner: Record auto originations lead to record delinquencies and a repossession glut. Give lenders a mortgage-style short sale for cars that recovers more than auction does.
ideas.customer: Credit unions and subprime and indirect auto lenders with rising 60-plus-day delinquencies.
ideas.problem: Auto originations hit a record $211B and auto delinquencies also hit a record (CNBC and others, Aug 2026). Lenders' only tool at scale is repossession and auction, which is slow, costly and yields discounted recoveries. Borrowers keep a deficiency balance and wrecked credit, and lenders lose more than a cooperative sale would cost them.
ideas.solution: At 45-60 days delinquent, the lender offers the borrower a lender-blessed voluntary sale. The platform lists the car at retail to dealers and private buyers, handles payoff letters, title and lien release in each state, and converts the shortfall into a small structured note or forgiveness within lender-set limits. The lender pays only when its net recovery beats projected repo loss.
ideas.why_now: Delinquencies at records, auction supply pressure, and credit unions with growing delinquent books and a reputation to protect. Mortgage short-sale playbooks are well understood, but nobody has ported them to autos.
ideas.revenue_model: Flat fee (about $500-$700) or 3-5% of sale price per completed sale, plus a performance share of recovery improvement over projected repo loss.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Lenders already lose money on repossession, but their servicing, collections and legal workflows are built around it, so no infrastructure exists to choreograph title, payoff and buyer across 50 states. The product is that plumbing.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with two or three credit unions with 5k-plus delinquent auto loans. Run a manual pilot in one state with a small dealer buyer network, comparing net recovery per unit against actual auction results. Use the data to sign a master services agreement.

ideas.title: AI-Use Attestation to Keep SMB Liability Cover
ideas.one_liner: As liability policies exclude generative AI, small firms need underwriter-ready proof of AI controls to win affirmative cover, and independent agencies need a renewal ritual that keeps them relevant.
ideas.customer: Independent insurance agencies (about 37k remain) that place GL and E&O for law firms, accountants, marketing agencies, clinics and contractors, plus those SMB clients.
ideas.problem: ISO's gen-AI exclusion is already on thousands of CGL policies (Insurance Business, 2026-09-16). AI-specialist insurers target tech firms, not a dental practice using an AI receptionist. Agencies can't advise and carriers haven't said what evidence they'd accept, so clients discover the gap at claim time.
ideas.solution: A lightweight AI Use Register: discover which AI tools staff use (SSO and browser discovery), apply policy templates and human-review logging, and output a standardized attestation that a panel of MGAs and carriers agree to accept for endorsements or premium credits. Agencies white-label it into their renewal workflow.
ideas.why_now: Exclusions are spreading now, independent agencies are shrinking (39k in 2024 to 37k in 2026, Insurance Journal) yet still sell 95% of commercial insurance through humans, and insurtech's dollars (99.1% of Q2 funding is AI-centric) go to back-office tools, not SMB risk evidence.
ideas.revenue_model: $49-$149 per month per SMB, billed via the agency or the client, plus MGA per-policy referral fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Carriers don't yet know what evidence they want, so whoever standardizes the artifact defines it, as cyber questionnaires and scans did for Coalition and At-Bay. Agencies get a reason to call every client at renewal.
ideas.first_30_days: Interview five underwriters on what evidence they'd accept. Ship a spreadsheet-and-form v0 of the register. Sell it to 10 agencies through state agent-association chapters and get 30 SMBs onto paid plans.

ideas.title: WhatsApp Tandas With Credit Reporting
ideas.one_liner: Felix proved WhatsApp-native finance at $8B of volume. Wrap the rotating savings groups that immigrant households already run in group chats with escrow, default cover and credit reporting.
ideas.customer: Latino, West African, Caribbean and South Asian households running tandas, susus and chit-fund-style rotating savings groups. The FDIC's 2023 survey counts 5.6M unbanked and 19M underbanked households, with minimum balances the top barrier.
ideas.problem: Rotating savings groups are the real financial system for many households, but they run on cash and trust, one bad organizer or defaulter breaks the pot, and the on-time payment history is invisible to credit bureaus. Cash-funded remittances now carry a 1% federal tax, nudging cash economies toward digital.
ideas.solution: A WhatsApp bot to create a tanda (amounts, order, schedule). Contributions are held in a partner-bank pass-through balance, or in stablecoin where appropriate, and payouts release on schedule. The organizer earns a fee, and a small guarantee pool covers late payers. On-time contributions are reported to bureaus as installment history through a furnisher partner.
ideas.why_now: Felix reached $8B cumulative volume with revenue up 2.5x on WhatsApp, the remittance tax pushes cash users to digital rails (Forbes, 2026-07-17), and stablecoin and bank-partner rails make small-balance escrow cheap.
ideas.revenue_model: 1-2% fee on each pot, $5 per month credit-building subscription, and lender referral fees for graduated members.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Don't replace the tanda, wrap it. The organizer is a trusted social underwriter with better default data than any bureau. The pooled payment history of organized groups becomes a proprietary dataset lenders will pay for.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 30 organizers via Spanish-language WhatsApp and Facebook groups, churches, taquerias and community organizations. Run 10 pilot tandas with manual escrow in a partner-bank sub-account at a 1.5% fee, and validate the credit-reporting path with a furnisher.

ideas.title: Nonrenewal Cure: Rebutting Insurer Cancellations
ideas.one_liner: Nonrenewal notices often cite fixable issues like roof condition, tree overhang or debris. Sell homeowners a fast diagnosis, repair and evidence packet to get re-underwritten instead of dumped on a FAIR plan.
ideas.customer: Homeowners in CA, FL, TX, CO, UT and NM who have received a nonrenewal notice, plus independent brokers who lose those clients.
ideas.problem: Nonrenewals are at records and homeowners have 30-75 days to react. Carriers are structurally conflicted about helping, and the FAIR plan is pricey with thin cover. Homeowners can't decode the reason code, can't tell which items are cheap to fix, and can't produce the evidence a carrier re-inspection accepts.
ideas.solution: Upload the notice. The service decodes the stated reason using state disclosure rules, dispatches vetted local contractors for the fix (patch, trim, vent screens), and produces a time-stamped photo and invoice packet. It files for reinspection or appeal, and gives the broker a clean file to re-market the risk. For wildfire-score cases it documents mitigation credits available under state rules.
ideas.why_now: Record nonrenewals, California passed three claims and nonrenewal bills on 2026-09-03, and insurance now rivals mortgage payments. Carriers rely more on aerial-imagery flags that homeowners rarely see or contest.
ideas.revenue_model: $149 diagnostic, $250-$500 evidence packet, 10-15% contractor referral fee, and broker referral fees on re-placed policies.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Many cancellations are cheap to cure, but the homeowner has no language, time or evidence, and the carrier won't help. A homeowner who has just been rescued becomes a lifetime referral source for brokers.
ideas.first_30_days: Post in local nonrenewal threads and neighborhood groups, and partner with three independent brokers. Handle 20 cases by hand, track how many carriers reinstate, and use the win rate to set pricing.

ideas.title: Positive Pay for Stablecoin Wallets
ideas.one_liner: Give mid-market finance teams the control environment auditors will demand before approving stablecoin flows: vendor wallet verification, sanctions and taint screening, and freeze-risk checks.
ideas.customer: Finance teams at $20M-$500M revenue companies starting to pay and receive USDC or USDT (via Citi and Coinbase, Stripe/Bridge or Circle), and the CPA and fractional-CFO firms that serve them.
ideas.problem: Stablecoin payments are irreversible, and wallet-address swaps and address poisoning are the new business email compromise. Companies inherit sanctions exposure (Senate Democrats allege about $2B of Iranian flows through Tether in a year). Funds received from a tainted wallet can be frozen. There is no bank-style 'positive pay' equivalent.
ideas.solution: Vendor wallet verification via signed challenge and callback, allowlist enforcement in the payment approval flow (Slack and email approvals), pre-payment counterparty screening, post-receipt taint checks, and NetSuite/QuickBooks reconciliation at the invoice level. Continuous behavioral KYC scoring, the gap flagged by The Block, is the roadmap.
ideas.why_now: Citi and Coinbase launched stablecoin acceptance with fiat settlement on 2026-09-28. Annual stablecoin volume tops $90T and doubled year on year, daily turnover is 0.78x, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
ideas.revenue_model: $500-$3,000 per month SaaS plus per-screen fees, sold through CPA and fractional-CFO channel partners.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Corporate adoption is gated by the controller's control environment, not by wallets. Positive Pay is a large business in traditional banking, and the wallet analog doesn't exist. Whoever ships the audit-ready control set becomes the default checklist.
ideas.first_30_days: Interview 25 controllers and CFOs with live or planned stablecoin flows. Ship a browser extension plus Slack approvals for wallet verification and allowlists. Sell $299 per month pilots through five CPA firms serving importers and crypto-adjacent SMEs.

ideas.title: Duty Refund Claims Desk for Small Importers
ideas.one_liner: Over $100B in tariff refunds are flowing, but small importers can't afford the paperwork. Run the filing, deadline tracking and refund advance as a service.
ideas.customer: Small and mid importers of record ($1M-$50M of annual imports) that paid the struck-down tariffs, plus customs brokers who don't want the grunt work.
ideas.problem: Refunds are flowing but small importers face records, liquidation and protest deadlines, multiple brokers and bonds, and filing costs ('not without a cost,' Colorado Sun, 2026-07-02). The government is fighting an order to refund all importers (WaPo, 2026-08-11). Brokers are paid per entry, not per refund, so nobody chases.
ideas.solution: Connect customs-entry data from the importer's broker, identify eligible entries and deadlines, file protests and post-summary corrections through a partner licensed customs broker, and track each claim to payment. Offer an advance of about 80% of approved claims at a discount, funded by a small credit facility.
ideas.why_now: Refunds have passed $100B (CNBC 2026-08-07, Forbes 2026-09-09) with litigation ongoing. Twenty-five states are challenging the replacement Section 122 tariffs, so a second claim wave may follow.
ideas.revenue_model: 10-15% success fee on recovered duties, plus a 2-3% monthly discount on advances once financing is in place.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck isn't law, it's data assembly and deadline hygiene. The refund often lands in a broker's account or gets stuck for lack of a clear owner. Small importers who recover cash are also the source of pass-through claims for the downstream-recovery business.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign a licensed customs broker as partner. Recruit 20 importers through marketplace-seller communities and manufacturer associations. Process five entries by hand end to end and collect the first success fees.

ideas.title: Compliance-as-Code for EWA and BNPL
ideas.one_liner: State-by-state earned wage access and BNPL rules are being written fast. Turn them into an API that checks fees, tips and disclosures before each product release.
ideas.customer: EWA and BNPL providers, payroll platforms and neobanks adding these features, and employers running EWA programs.
ideas.problem: Colorado sued EarnIn (2026-09-08), Maryland banned EWA tipping, and New York and Illinois have BNPL rules. Each state differs on fees, tips, disclosures and licensing. Product managers ship copy and fee configs faster than lawyers can review them.
ideas.solution: A rules engine and configuration API. Providers submit product configs (fees, tip prompts, speed, limits) and get per-state pass/fail, required disclosure text, and a change log. It also monitors new bills and enforcement actions and produces exam-ready evidence.
ideas.why_now: Enforcement began in Sept 2026 and legislatures are still moving. Providers need pre-release checks now and will need audit trails when examiners arrive.
ideas.revenue_model: $3k-$10k per month per provider, with per-state add-ons and content licensing to law firms.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: EWA's legal risk sits in UI copy and fee configuration, which product teams change weekly. Rules-as-code plugs into release management, which a law-firm memo never can.
ideas.first_30_days: Publish a free 12-state EWA and BNPL rule tracker as a lead magnet. Pair with a fintech law firm and pitch five mid-size providers and payroll platforms on a $3k per month pilot.

ideas.title: FinOps for Open-Banking Data Spend
ideas.one_liner: Bank data access is turning into a metered cost. Do for aggregator bills what cloud FinOps did for AWS bills.
ideas.customer: Fintech lenders, budgeting apps and payroll and EWA apps spending $200k-$10M per year on aggregators (Plaid, MX, Finicity) and direct bank APIs.
ideas.problem: The CFPB 1033 rule is stayed, and a rewrite sent to OIRA on 2026-08-06 may let banks charge aggregators past a free-request threshold (PYMNTS). Developers over-poll accounts and pay per connection and per refresh, and a fee threshold would create sudden bill shock. Nobody owns the cost line.
ideas.solution: A proxy and observability layer that dedupes and caches pulls, replaces polling with webhooks and event-based refreshes, refreshes only when a decision needs fresh data (underwriting, payday), benchmarks vendor mix and price, and forecasts spend under proposed fee scenarios.
ideas.why_now: Regulatory uncertainty is at its peak, states like New York are proposing their own regimes, and fintechs face margin pressure. Any fee threshold in the rewrite turns data access into variable cost of goods sold.
ideas.revenue_model: 15-20% of verified savings (gainshare) or $2k-$10k per month SaaS.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Data-access cost is becoming a real COGS line that finance teams can't yet see. My hypothesis is that dedupe and smarter refresh timing alone save 20-40%, so the first step is an audit that verifies it. A fee threshold makes that savings pool bigger.
ideas.first_30_days: Offer a free aggregator bill audit to 20 fintechs (they share invoices and usage exports). Quantify wasteful pulls, convert two to a 15% gainshare agreement, and publish the anonymized benchmark.

ideas.title: Loss-Draft as a Service for Servicers
ideas.one_liner: After a hail or wildfire claim, insurer money is trapped in slow servicer loss-draft processes. Digitize milestone releases so contractors get paid in days, not months.
ideas.customer: Mortgage servicers' loss-draft departments, and roofing and repair contractors who work insurance claims.
ideas.problem: Insurance claim checks are co-payable to the mortgage lender. Servicers hold the funds and release them in draws after inspections, taking weeks to months. Contractors demand money upfront, homeowners run out of patience, and disputes spread (State Farm hail-claim lawsuits are widening from Oklahoma).
ideas.solution: Digital loss-draft. The homeowner uploads the claim payment, funds sit in a servicer-controlled escrow, and milestone releases are verified via geo-tagged photo and video review. Contractors are paid instantly via RTP or FedNow, and the servicer gets a compliance dashboard on cycle times.
ideas.why_now: Claim disputes are surging and State Farm is adding 3,000 claims staff (Insurance Journal, 2026-09-25). Instant rails are mature, and servicers face regulatory scrutiny on loss-mitigation timelines (verify the specific rules).
ideas.revenue_model: $150-$400 per claim from the servicer, or 0.5-1.0% of proceeds, plus a 1% instant-pay fee to contractors.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Servicers hold large claim balances but run loss-draft as a paper-heavy cost center. Contractors accept lower prices for fast, certain payment, which also lowers repair cost and dispute rates.
ideas.first_30_days: Approach five mid-size servicers' loss-draft heads with a free diagnostic on average days to disbursement. Sign a pilot for one catastrophe event. Recruit roofing contractor associations in hail-prone states to onboard.

ideas.title: Credit Union Tokenized Deposit Network
ideas.one_liner: Give thousands of small credit unions a shared 24/7 tokenized-deposit settlement network so they can answer the 'war for deposits' together instead of losing it one by one.
ideas.customer: Credit unions ($500M-$10B assets), state leagues and CUSOs, and later their members and local merchants.
ideas.problem: Banks describe the stablecoin fight as a '$6 trillion war for deposits' (CoinDesk, 2026-09-14). No single credit union has the scale to run its own token or build 24/7 settlement, and Zelle-style networks are controlled by big banks. Members get weekday-hours payments between institutions.
ideas.solution: A CUSO-owned network of tokenized member deposits (not a stablecoin at first), starting with 24/7 credit-union-to-credit-union settlement for shared branching and member P2P, then bill pay and merchant acceptance. A licensed trust-bank or custody partner handles the token layer and reserves.
ideas.why_now: The OCC charter wave (Circle 2026-07-10, Coinbase April, Bridge and Crypto.com conditional) has made compliant token infrastructure available to partner with. Citi and Coinbase launched corporate stablecoin acceptance on 2026-09-28, and the GENIUS Act takes effect around Jan 2027 (verify).
ideas.revenue_model: Network transaction fees, SaaS to member credit unions, and a share of reserve income on the settlement layer.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The cooperative structure is the unfair advantage. Credit unions already share ATMs, branching and core processing through CUSOs, so a shared money layer is a natural extension that gives 4,500 small institutions scale none could build alone.
ideas.first_30_days: Get LOIs from five credit unions through one state league. Run a paper pilot for inter-credit-union treasury settlement with a partner trust bank, and charge pilot fees for design work and integration.

ideas.title: Disaster-Day Instant Cash Parametric Cover
ideas.one_liner: Pay a fixed sum to a household's phone within hours of an official evacuation order or multi-day power shutoff, funded by cheap capital that is hunting for granular parametric risk.
ideas.customer: Employers, HOAs, utilities, school districts and credit unions in wildfire, flood and hurricane zones that buy group cover for employees or members. Also mortgage servicers for at-risk borrowers.
ideas.problem: After an evacuation order, households spend hundreds of dollars a day on hotels, fuel, food and pet boarding before any additional-living-expense claim is paid. Renters and FAIR plan or nonrenewed homeowners often lack that cover entirely. Claims take weeks.
ideas.solution: A parametric micro-policy paying $500-$2,000 within hours when an official evacuation order, extended power shutoff, or verified flood depth covers the insured address. Triggers come from public alert feeds and utility notices, and payment goes to a debit card or wallet. An MGA fronts it with ILS-backed capacity.
ideas.why_now: Reinsurance is softening and cat bond capital is at a record ($65.6B outstanding), so granular parametric capacity is cheap. Instant rails are mature, and nonrenewals and FAIR plan reliance are growing.
ideas.revenue_model: $5-$15 per household per month, an MGA margin of 20-30%, and group distribution fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Instant cash, not indemnity, is the product, and small payouts make basis risk tolerable. Institutions with a duty of care buy per head, so a single sale reaches hundreds of households.
ideas.first_30_days: Pilot with a rural credit union and one WUI-county employer or school district. Find a parametric MGA to front it, run a synthetic-trigger payout test, and sign a paid 90-day pilot.

ideas.title: Gig Income Shock Cover From Pooled Data
ideas.one_liner: Insure the algorithm: pay drivers when they are deactivated or when regional platform earnings collapse, using pooled earnings data to defeat moral hazard.
ideas.customer: Rideshare and delivery drivers through driver co-ops, forums and earnings-tracking apps, and credit unions that finance drivers' cars.
ideas.problem: A deactivation or algorithmic pay cut can remove 30-100% of a driver's income overnight with no unemployment insurance, while record auto delinquencies (brief) mean many drivers carry stressed car loans. Individual income insurance has historically failed on moral hazard and adverse selection.
ideas.solution: A membership cover paying 2-4 weeks of trailing average earnings on (a) a verified platform deactivation, or (b) a regional earnings-per-hour index falling more than 25% against baseline, computed from pooled, driver-consented earnings data. Structure it through a fronting carrier or discretionary mutual, and offer credit unions a car-payment protection version.
ideas.why_now: Record auto delinquencies, growing algorithmic management of pay, driver data cooperatives and earnings-tracking apps that already pool consented data, and instant payout rails.
ideas.revenue_model: $10-$20 per month premium, credit-union-paid group premium bundled with car loans, and anonymized index data licensing.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Moral hazard is the classic reason income insurance fails, but a platform-controlled event (deactivation) and a pooled regional index are not something the worker can game. The data cooperatives already exist and are the missing underwriting input.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with one driver co-op or large forum for a 300-member paid pilot with a capped reserve. Collect earnings-data consents, back-test the index triggers on historical data, and have a fronting partner review the structure.

ideas.title: Mini Cat Bonds for Co-ops and Counties
ideas.one_liner: Cat bond capital is at record highs but deals under $50M are uneconomic. Make a $5-25M cat bond a 90-day, low-cost, template product for the sponsors the market ignores.
ideas.customer: Small public risk pools, rural electric cooperatives, counties, hospital systems and small regional insurers needing $5M-$50M of catastrophe protection.
ideas.problem: Cat bond issuance is a record $18.9B year to date with $65.6B outstanding, yet legal, modeling, rating and SPV costs of $1M-plus put small deals out of reach. Small sponsors stay in the traditional market or go bare, while primary property markets stay hard.
ideas.solution: A standardized private cat bond or collateralized reinsurance template: pre-approved documents, standard parametric triggers with an independent calculation agent, treasury-fund collateral with transparent accounting, and a target all-in cost under $150k with issuance in about 90 days. Sell the notes to ILS funds seeking diversification.
ideas.why_now: Record traditional and ILS capital, softening through 2027 (Jefferies), and mature tokenized and money-market collateral (Goldman put a $100B Treasury fund into crypto plumbing, CoinDesk 2026-09-28). ILS investors want diversification beyond Florida wind.
ideas.revenue_model: 1.5-3% of limit as a structuring fee, plus annual administration and calculation-agent fees.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Softening means capital wants to deploy, so the binding constraint is deal cost per dollar of limit. That is a documentation and operations problem, not a risk-appetite problem.
ideas.first_30_days: Retain an offshore law firm and a calculation agent. Find two state pooling associations with wildfire or hail exposure, get indications of interest from two ILS funds, and produce a reusable term-sheet template. Charge a structuring retainer to fund first-deal work.

ideas.title: Stablecoin Depeg and Freeze Cover
ideas.one_liner: GENIUS made stablecoins legal, not insured. Sell corporate treasurers parametric cover for issuer depeg, redemption suspension and wallet freezes so their risk committees will approve holding balances.
ideas.customer: Treasurers and CFOs at mid-market and payments companies holding $1M-$100M in USDC or USDT, including corporate clients of the new Citi and Coinbase flow.
ideas.problem: GENIUS gives holders priority claims but no deposit insurance. USDT is about $140B and USDC about $74B, the Senate Democrats' Tether report alleges $2B of Iranian flows against $550M frozen, and Bitcoin has drawn down about 50%. Auditors and risk committees want risk transfer, and there is none.
